SELECT 
  fish_date_doy,
  cls,
  COUNT(DISTINCT boat) as boats,
  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  SUM(anglers) as total_anglers,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::float / SUM(anglers), 2) as yt_per_angler,
  ROUND(AVG(yt), 2) as avg_yt_per_trip
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 6 
  AND fish_date_doy >= 60 
  AND fish_date_doy <= 86
  AND cls IN ('overnight', 'day_1_5', 'three_quarter')
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls
LIMIT 100;

SELECT 
  fish_date_doy,
  boat,
  cls,
  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  SUM(anglers) as total_anglers,
  COUNT(*) as num_trips,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::float / SUM(anglers), 2) as yt_per_angler
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 6 
  AND fish_date_doy >= 100 
  AND fish_date_doy <= 115
  AND cls IN ('overnight', 'day_1_5', 'three_quarter')
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, boat, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy DESC, yt_per_angler DESC
LIMIT 100;

import pandas as pd

# Get boat rankings for season 6
trips = tables['trips']
s6_trips = trips[trips['fish_date_season'] == 6]

# Filter for relevant classes
relevant_classes = ['overnight', 'day_1_5', 'three_quarter']
s6_relevant = s6_trips[s6_trips['cls'].isin(relevant_classes)]

# Calculate boat performance
boat_perf = s6_relevant.groupby('boat').agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'boat': 'count'
}).rename(columns={'boat': 'num_trips'})

boat_perf['yt_per_angler'] = boat_perf['yt'] / boat_perf['anglers']
boat_perf = boat_perf.sort_values('yt_per_angler', ascending=False)

print("Season 6 Boat Rankings (D60-121, multi-day and 3Q):")
print(boat_perf.head(15))
print("\n")

# Also look at the peaks we missed - D60-D86 vs D100-D115
early_peak = s6_relevant[(s6_relevant['fish_date_doy'] >= 60) & (s6_relevant['fish_date_doy'] <= 86)]
mid_peak = s6_relevant[(s6_relevant['fish_date_doy'] >= 100) & (s6_relevant['fish_date_doy'] <= 115)]
